/* PC5251 shared drawing core — window.PC.
   Generic theme, colour, canvas, axes, interaction, tooltip, linked-state and
   accessible table-twin primitives. Component renderers live in panels/;
   page-level behaviour lives in page.js. Dependency-free classic script. */

(function (global) {
  "use strict";

  var root = document.documentElement;
  var live = null;                       // live CSSStyleDeclaration; values track the theme

  /* ── extension ── legacy → canonical token map. Pages declare these as CSS
     compat aliases; this map is the belt-and-braces fallback for pages that
     have not been migrated yet, so a stale token never resolves to "". ────── */
  var ALIAS = {
    "--bg": "--page",
    "--panel": "--surface-1",
    "--ink": "--text-primary",
    "--ink2": "--text-secondary",
    "--ink3": "--muted",
    "--line": "--grid",
    "--line2": "--axis",
    "--surface": "--surface-1",
    "--text": "--text-primary",
    "--secondary": "--text-secondary",
    "--accent": "--series-1",
    "--baseline": "--axis",
    "--sel-ring": "--series-1",
    "--science-bg": "--surface-2",
    "--science-border": "--axis"
  };

  /* ── ported: master (const V) + superconductor (function css) ───────────── */
  function css(name) {
    if (!live) live = getComputedStyle(root);
    var v = live.getPropertyValue(name).trim();
    if (!v && ALIAS[name]) v = live.getPropertyValue(ALIAS[name]).trim();
    return v;
  }

  /* ══ theme ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

  var MQ_DARK = "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)";

  /* ── ported: master (isDark) ── data-theme first, matchMedia second ─────── */
  function isDark() {
    var t = root.getAttribute("data-theme");
    if (t === "dark") return true;
    if (t === "light") return false;
    return matchMedia(MQ_DARK).matches;      // no attribute → follow the system
  }

  /* ── extension ── the write half of the same 3-way resolution ──────────── */
  function setTheme(t) {
    if (t === "dark" || t === "light") root.setAttribute("data-theme", t);
    else root.removeAttribute("data-theme");   // null / "system" → back to matchMedia
    return t;
  }

  /* Generic theme repaint subscription. Component modules register their own
     paint collections; the drawing core never needs to know component names. */
  var themePainters = [];
  function registerThemePainter(paint) {
    if (typeof paint !== "function") throw new TypeError("registerThemePainter expects a function");
    if (themePainters.indexOf(paint) < 0) themePainters.push(paint);
    return function () {
      var at = themePainters.indexOf(paint);
      if (at >= 0) themePainters.splice(at, 1);
    };
  }
  function repaintThemePainters() {
    themePainters.slice().forEach(function (paint) { paint(); });
  }

  /* ══ typography ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     ── extension ── ONE constant pair for every canvas label in the suite.
     The family is resolved from --font at call time, so changing the token
     (or the theme) reaches chart labels without touching any chart code. ─── */
  var FONT_SIZE = { tick: "10px", emph: "600 11.5px" };
  var FONT_FALLBACK = 'system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif';
  function fontFamily() { return css("--font") || FONT_FALLBACK; }
  function tickFont() { return FONT_SIZE.tick + " " + fontFamily(); }
  function emphFont() { return FONT_SIZE.emph + " " + fontFamily(); }

  /* ══ colour ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

  /* ── ported: master (RAMP, hex2rgb, rampColor) ── validated ramp:
     light 250→700, dark anchor-flipped 600→100 ───────────────────────────── */
  var RAMP = ["--ramp-0", "--ramp-1", "--ramp-2", "--ramp-3", "--ramp-4"];
  function hex2rgb(h) {
    return [1, 3, 5].map(function (i) { return parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16); });
  }
  function mixStops(steps, t) {
    t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, t));
    var x = t * (steps.length - 1);
    var i = Math.min(Math.floor(x), steps.length - 2);
    var f = x - i;
    var a = steps[i], b = steps[i + 1];
    return "rgb(" + Math.round(a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * f) + "," +
                    Math.round(a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * f) + "," +
                    Math.round(a[2] + (b[2] - a[2]) * f) + ")";
  }
  /* ── extension ── stops resolved once; the design-matrix panels issue tens of
     thousands of fills per repaint and cannot afford a lookup per cell. ───── */
  function rampScale() {
    var steps = RAMP.map(function (n) { return hex2rgb(css(n)); });
    return function (t) { return mixStops(steps, t); };
  }
  function rampColor(t) { return rampScale()(t); }

  /* ── extension ── the "heat" ramp: --heat-0..4, matplotlib plasma. A SECOND
     sequential encoder, interpolated exactly as rampColor is (same mixStops,
     same five anchors, same clamp). It is for an UNSIGNED INTENSITY read on a
     SPATIAL LAYOUT — a detector map, an image, a pixel grid — where the house
     ramp's single hue spends its whole range on lightness and the layout's own
     structure goes with it. Everything else stays on rampColor: this is not a
     replacement, and a page picks one encoder per quantity, never both. ───── */
  var HEAT = ["--heat-0", "--heat-1", "--heat-2", "--heat-3", "--heat-4"];
  function heatScale() {
    var steps = HEAT.map(function (n) { return hex2rgb(css(n)); });
    return function (t) { return mixStops(steps, t); };
  }
  function heatColor(t) { return heatScale()(t); }

  /* ── ported: master (s2l, l2s, toOklab, fromOklab, divColor) — exact
     coefficients; diverging arms are interpolated in OKLab so the midpoint
     never turns muddy. ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  var s2l = function (c) { return c <= 0.04045 ? c / 12.92 : Math.pow((c + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4); };
  var l2s = function (c) {
    c = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, c));
    return c <= 0.0031308 ? 12.92 * c : 1.055 * Math.pow(c, 1 / 2.4) - 0.055;
  };
  function toOklab(hex) {
    var rgb = hex2rgb(hex).map(function (v) { return s2l(v / 255); });
    var r = rgb[0], g = rgb[1], b = rgb[2];
    var l = Math.cbrt(0.4122214708 * r + 0.5363325363 * g + 0.0514459929 * b);
    var m = Math.cbrt(0.2119034982 * r + 0.6806995451 * g + 0.1073969566 * b);
    var s = Math.cbrt(0.0883024619 * r + 0.2817188376 * g + 0.6299787005 * b);
    return [0.2104542553 * l + 0.7936177850 * m - 0.0040720468 * s,
            1.9779984951 * l - 2.4285922050 * m + 0.4505937099 * s,
            0.0259040371 * l + 0.7827717662 * m - 0.8086757660 * s];
  }
  function fromOklab(L) {
    var l = Math.pow(L[0] + 0.3963377774 * L[1] + 0.2158037573 * L[2], 3);
    var m = Math.pow(L[0] - 0.1055613458 * L[1] - 0.0638541728 * L[2], 3);
    var s = Math.pow(L[0] - 0.0894841775 * L[1] - 1.2914855480 * L[2], 3);
    var rgb = [4.0767416621 * l - 3.3077115913 * m + 0.2309699292 * s,
              -1.2684380046 * l + 2.6097574011 * m - 0.3413193965 * s,
              -0.0041960863 * l - 0.7034186147 * m + 1.7076147010 * s]
      .map(function (v) { return Math.round(l2s(v) * 255); });
    return "rgb(" + rgb[0] + "," + rgb[1] + "," + rgb[2] + ")";
  }
  /* ── extension ── anchors resolved once, same shape as rampScale ────────── */
  function divScale() {
    var mid = toOklab(css("--div-mid"));
    var pos = toOklab(css("--div-pos"));
    var neg = toOklab(css("--div-neg"));
    return function (r) {
      var t = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, r || 0));
      var b = t >= 0 ? pos : neg;
      var f = Math.abs(t);
      return fromOklab([0, 1, 2].map(function (k) { return mid[k] + (b[k] - mid[k]) * f; }));
    };
  }
  function divColor(r) { return divScale()(r); }

  /* ── ported: master (inkOn) ── a label inside a filled cell picks ink or
     white by the fill's own luminance, independently of the page theme. ──── */
  function inkOn(rgbStr) {
    var m = String(rgbStr).match(/\d+/g) || [0, 0, 0];
    var v = m.map(function (x) { return s2l(x / 255); });
    return (0.2126 * v[0] + 0.7152 * v[1] + 0.0722 * v[2]) > 0.42 ? "#0b0b0b" : "#ffffff";
  }

  /* ══ canvas geometry ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

  /* ── ported: master (fit), with superconductor's measure-the-box fallback
     when w/h are omitted (its canvases are CSS-sized, the master's are not) ─ */
  function fit(cv, w, h) {
    if (w == null || h == null) {
      var rect = cv.getBoundingClientRect();
      w = w == null ? Math.max(280, rect.width) : w;
      h = h == null ? Math.max(160, rect.height) : h;
    }
    var dpr = Math.min(global.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);
    cv.width = Math.round(w * dpr);
    cv.height = Math.round(h * dpr);
    cv.style.width = w + "px";
    cv.style.height = h + "px";
    var g = cv.getContext("2d");
    g.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);
    g.clearRect(0, 0, w, h);
    return g;
  }

  /* ── ported: master (PAD, scales, frame, tickText, fmt, extent, pad10) ─── */
  var PAD = { l: 26, r: 10, t: 10, b: 20 };
  function scales(cv, xr, yr, pad) {
    var p = pad || PAD;
    var w = parseFloat(cv.style.width) || cv.getBoundingClientRect().width;
    var h = parseFloat(cv.style.height) || cv.getBoundingClientRect().height;
    var iw = w - p.l - p.r, ih = h - p.t - p.b;
    return {
      x: function (v) { return p.l + (v - xr[0]) / (xr[1] - xr[0]) * iw; },
      y: function (v) { return p.t + ih - (v - yr[0]) / (yr[1] - yr[0]) * ih; },
      w: w, h: h, iw: iw, ih: ih, p: p
    };
  }
  /* ── extension ── bridge: master's scales geometry → superconductor's box ─ */
  function boxOf(s) {
    return { left: s.p.l, right: s.p.l + s.iw, top: s.p.t, bottom: s.p.t + s.ih };
  }
  function frame(g, s) {
    g.strokeStyle = css("--grid");
    g.lineWidth = 1;
    g.strokeRect(s.p.l + 0.5, s.p.t + 0.5, s.iw - 1, s.ih - 1);
  }
  function tickText(g, txt, x, y, align, baseline) {
    g.fillStyle = css("--muted");
    g.font = tickFont();                       // re-keyed onto the one font pair
    g.textAlign = align || "center";
    g.textBaseline = baseline || "top";
    g.fillText(txt, x, y);
  }
  var fmt = function (v) {
    return Math.abs(v) >= 1000 ? v.toFixed(0) : Math.abs(v) >= 10 ? v.toFixed(0) : v.toFixed(1);
  };
  function extent(a, mask) {
    var lo = Infinity, hi = -Infinity;
    for (var i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
      if (mask && !mask[i]) continue;
      if (a[i] < lo) lo = a[i];
      if (a[i] > hi) hi = a[i];
    }
    if (!isFinite(lo)) return [0, 1];
    if (lo === hi) { lo -= 1; hi += 1; }
    return [lo, hi];
  }
  function pad10(r) { var d = (r[1] - r[0]) * 0.06; return [r[0] - d, r[1] + d]; }

  /* ── ported: master (quantile) ── linear interpolation on a sorted array ── */
  function quantile(sorted, q) {
    var p = (sorted.length - 1) * q, lo = Math.floor(p), hi = Math.ceil(p);
    return sorted[lo] + (sorted[hi] - sorted[lo]) * (p - lo);
  }

  /* ══ axes ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     ── ported: superconductor (drawAxes) ── same renderer, re-keyed:
       gridlines   --grid          (was --grid)
       tick labels --muted         (was --muted)
       spines      --axis          (was --secondary — spines are structure, not text)
       axis titles --text-secondary(was --secondary)
       fonts       PC.font.tick()/emph() (was a hard-coded 11px system-ui)
     Extensions kept deliberately small: arg 2 may be a PC.scales object (then
     xScale/yScale default to its mappers), and a trailing opts object controls
     tick formatting, which gridlines to draw, and the spines. Default tick
     label is String(v) for integers and PC.fmt(v) otherwise, so a computed
     midpoint never renders as 0.30000000000000004. ───────────────────────── */
  function drawAxes(g, box, xTicks, yTicks, xScale, yScale, xLabel, yLabel, opts) {
    var s = null;
    if (box && box.p && typeof box.x === "function") { s = box; box = boxOf(s); }
    if (typeof xScale !== "function" && s) xScale = s.x;
    if (typeof yScale !== "function" && s) yScale = s.y;
    opts = opts || {};
    var defFmt = function (v) {
      return typeof v === "number" && !Number.isInteger(v) ? fmt(v) : String(v);
    };
    var xFmt = opts.xFmt || opts.fmt || defFmt;
    var yFmt = opts.yFmt || opts.fmt || defFmt;
    var grid = opts.grid === undefined ? "both" : opts.grid;
    var wantX = grid === true || grid === "both" || grid === "x";
    var wantY = grid === true || grid === "both" || grid === "y";

    g.font = tickFont();
    g.textAlign = "start";
    g.textBaseline = "alphabetic";
    g.lineWidth = 1;

    (xTicks || []).forEach(function (value) {
      var x = xScale(value);
      if (wantX) {
        g.strokeStyle = css("--grid");
        g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(x + 0.5, box.top); g.lineTo(x + 0.5, box.bottom); g.stroke();
      }
      g.fillStyle = css("--muted");
      var label = xFmt(value);
      g.fillText(label, x - g.measureText(label).width / 2, box.bottom + 18);
    });

    (yTicks || []).forEach(function (value) {
      var y = yScale(value);
      if (wantY) {
        g.strokeStyle = css("--grid");
        g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(box.left, y + 0.5); g.lineTo(box.right, y + 0.5); g.stroke();
      }
      g.fillStyle = css("--muted");
      var label = yFmt(value);
      g.fillText(label, box.left - g.measureText(label).width - 7, y + 4);
    });

    if (opts.spines !== false) {
      g.strokeStyle = css("--axis");
      g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(box.left, box.bottom + 0.5); g.lineTo(box.right, box.bottom + 0.5); g.stroke();
      g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(box.left + 0.5, box.top); g.lineTo(box.left + 0.5, box.bottom); g.stroke();
    }

    g.font = emphFont();
    g.fillStyle = css("--text-secondary");
    if (xLabel) {
      g.fillText(xLabel, (box.left + box.right) / 2 - g.measureText(xLabel).width / 2, box.bottom + 38);
    }
    if (yLabel) {
      g.save();
      g.translate(opts.yTitleX == null ? 13 : opts.yTitleX,
                  (box.top + box.bottom) / 2 + g.measureText(yLabel).width / 2);
      g.rotate(-Math.PI / 2);
      g.fillText(yLabel, 0, 0);
      g.restore();
    }
    g.font = tickFont();
  }

  /* ══ hover ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     ── ported: master (attachHover registry) ── generalised: the point list,
     the mask and the callbacks are supplied per canvas instead of read from
     module globals, and re-calling hover() on an already-bound canvas just
     refreshes them (the master's `if (cv.dataset.hooked) return`). Hit radius
     is at least 24px — the dot is 4px, the target is a finger. ───────────── */
  function normalizePts(pts) {
    var out = [];
    if (!pts) return out;
    for (var k = 0; k < pts.length; k++) {
      var p = pts[k];
      if (!p) continue;
      if (typeof p.length === "number") out.push([p[0], p[1], p.length > 2 ? p[2] : k]);
      else out.push([p.x, p.y, p.i == null ? k : p.i]);
    }
    return out;
  }

  /* ══ touch mode ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     ── extension, appended 2026-08-31 ── The defect the owner reported from a
     REAL handset: a hover readout is useless on a phone. PC.tip places #tip at
     clientX+14 / clientY+14 — under the very finger that summoned it — and
     pointerleave fires the instant that finger lifts, so the reader never gets
     to read it; meanwhile base.css's `canvas{touch-action:none}` was taking
     the scroll gesture away from the page, so a chart was also a dead zone the
     reader could not scroll out of.

     GATED ON INPUT CAPABILITY, NEVER ON WIDTH. `(hover: none) and
     (pointer: coarse)` is true for a finger and false for a mouse whatever the
     viewport is, so a narrow desktop window keeps the mouse path and a large
     tablet gets the touch path. Re-read on `change`, so a plugged-in mouse
     switches the page back mid-session.

     WHAT TOUCH MODE DOES, in one paragraph. A `pointermove` from a touch
     pointer is ignored — that gesture now belongs to the browser (base.css
     ships `touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom`), and a hover readout dragged along
     under the finger was the defect. A `click` — the tap — selects the nearest
     point within max(32, opts.radius) and fires the panel's own `onHit`
     exactly as a mouse hover does, ALSO firing its `onClick` if it registered
     one, because a tap is both. While that `onHit` runs, PC.tip() is
     redirected into a `.pc-readout` strip docked directly BELOW the chart, in
     the same plot box, instead of the floating #tip — so the payload the demo
     already writes is what the reader sees, out from under their finger and
     still there after the lift — and a `.pc-mark` ring is placed over the
     canvas at the hit point so they can see which point it is about. (Below,
     not above: above put the strip under the ⤢ button, which is anchored to
     the box's top-right corner. See readoutFor.) A tap on empty space clears
     both and fires `onLeave`. Tapping the SAME point again re-selects it: the
     readout refreshes and the ring stays. It never toggles off, for the same
     reason a second mouse click on one point does nothing surprising today —
     a reader who taps a point twice is asking to see it, not to lose it.

     THE MOUSE PATH IS UNCHANGED, deliberately down to WHICH canvases react to
     a click. Touch mode needs the click listener bound on every canvas (the
     `if (st.bound) return handle;` guard below runs before the old
     `typeof opts.onClick === "function"` test, so a canvas whose first call
     omitted onClick could never acquire a listener later), and binding it
     unconditionally must not make a canvas newly clickable with a MOUSE. So
     the old test is frozen at first-bind time into `st.clickable`, and the
     mouse branch obeys that flag and nothing else. ────────────────────────── */

  var TOUCH_MQ = "(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)";
  var touchMode = false;
  try { touchMode = !!(global.matchMedia && global.matchMedia(TOUCH_MQ).matches); }
  catch (e) { touchMode = false; }
  (function () {
    var mq = null;
    try { mq = global.matchMedia ? global.matchMedia(TOUCH_MQ) : null; } catch (e) { return; }
    if (!mq) return;
    function onChange() {
      var next = false;
      try { next = !!mq.matches; } catch (e) { next = false; }
      if (next === touchMode) return;
      touchMode = next;
      if (!touchMode) clearTapSel();     // a mouse arrived: the docked readout goes
    }
    if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener("change", onChange);
    else if (mq.addListener) mq.addListener(onChange);
  })();

  /* The plot box: the SAME wrapper list the phone chart overlay picks for its
     ⤢ button (that module now calls through here), so the button, the docked
     readout and the ring always land in one container — which is also what
     makes them work unchanged inside the full-screen overlay, because the
     overlay promotes exactly this box. */
  var PLOT_BOXES = ".pbox,.chartbox,.plotwrap,.bookbox,.plot-card,.dm,.mxcard,.scard";
  function plotBoxOf(cv) {
    if (!cv) return null;
    var b = cv.closest ? cv.closest(PLOT_BOXES) : null;
    return b || cv.parentElement;
  }

  var tapSel = null;        // {canvas,st,box,i,readout,mark} — ONE per page
  var tapInto = null;       // non-null while a tap's onHit runs: tip() docks

  function raf(fn) {
    (global.requestAnimationFrame || function (f) { return setTimeout(f, 16); })(fn);
  }
  function childByClass(box, cls) {
    var kids = box.children, i;
    for (i = 0; i < kids.length; i++) if (kids[i].className === cls) return kids[i];
    return null;
  }
  /* DOCKED BELOW THE CANVAS — a caption under the chart, not a bar over it.
     Corrected 2026-08-31 after the owner's phone screenshot: the strip was
     first inserted as the box's FIRST child, and that put it under the ⤢
     button, which is absolutely positioned at the BOX's top:4px/right:4px
     (components.css §23D). The button then rendered on the strip's top-right
     corner, clipped at the box edge instead of sitting on the chart — the
     owner's words, "the full screen button is at a wrong space". Reserving
     52px of padding for it (the first attempt) fixed the text collision but
     not the button's PLACE, which is the actual defect.

     Below the canvas there is no conflict at all: the button is back over the
     drawing area where it has always been, and the chart no longer jumps down
     by the strip's own height on the first tap — the point the reader just
     touched stays exactly where their finger was.

     The strip is inserted after the box's own direct child that CONTAINS the
     canvas, not after the canvas itself: a demo may wrap its canvas
     (.imgframe, .chartbox), and the strip belongs to the box as a sibling of
     that wrapper rather than inside it.

     role=status + aria-live: the same tap announces the payload to a screen
     reader. */
  function readoutFor(sel) {
    if (sel.readout && sel.readout.isConnected) return sel.readout;
    var el = childByClass(sel.box, "pc-readout");
    if (!el) {
      el = document.createElement("div");
      el.className = "pc-readout";
      el.setAttribute("role", "status");
      el.setAttribute("aria-live", "polite");
      var anchor = sel.canvas;
      while (anchor && anchor.parentNode !== sel.box) anchor = anchor.parentNode;
      sel.box.insertBefore(el, anchor ? anchor.nextSibling : null);
    }
    sel.readout = el;
    return el;
  }
  /* A tap near the bottom of the screen can put the strip below the fold. Bring
     it in by the MINIMUM amount and only then: block:"nearest" aligns it to the
     viewport's BOTTOM edge, so the sticky tab strip (46px) and the parameter
     bar (44px) — both pinned at the TOP — are never in the way, and a strip
     that is already visible is not moved at all, so an ordinary tap never
     scrolls the page under the reader. Inside the full-screen overlay the page
     itself is scroll-locked and the same call scrolls the overlay's own
     container, which is what should happen there. */
  function revealReadout(sel) {
    var el = sel && sel.readout;
    if (!el || !el.isConnected) return;
    var r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    var vh = global.innerHeight || 0;
    if (r.top >= 0 && r.bottom <= vh) return;
    try { el.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest", inline: "nearest" }); }
    catch (e) { try { el.scrollIntoView(false); } catch (e2) {} }
  }
  /* A DOM ring, not a canvas draw: no demo's draw code changes, the mark
     survives the redraw a tap's own onClick triggers, and it re-themes itself
     from --accent like every other piece of chrome. */
  function markFor(sel) {
    if (sel.mark && sel.mark.isConnected) return sel.mark;
    var el = childByClass(sel.box, "pc-mark");
    if (!el) {
      el = document.createElement("div");
      el.className = "pc-mark";
      el.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");   // the readout carries the meaning
      sel.box.appendChild(el);
    }
    sel.box.classList.add("pc-plotbox");        // the ring's containing block
    sel.mark = el;
    return el;
  }
  function placeMark(sel, p) {
    var el = markFor(sel);
    var cr = sel.canvas.getBoundingClientRect(), br = sel.box.getBoundingClientRect();
    el.style.left = (cr.left - br.left + p[0]) + "px";
    el.style.top = (cr.top - br.top + p[1]) + "px";
  }
  function fireOn(st, name, a, b, c, d) {
    var f = st && st.opts && st.opts[name];
    if (typeof f !== "function") return null;
    return f(a, b, c, d);
  }
  function pointOf(st, i) {
    var list = (st && st.pts) || [];
    for (var k = 0; k < list.length; k++) if (list[k][2] === i) return list[k];
    return null;
  }
  /* Clearing runs the panel's OWN onLeave first, with tip() still docked — so
     a panel that clears by calling PC.hideTip() (which is nearly all of them)
     takes its strip down through the path it already has — and only then
     removes whatever is left. */
  function clearTapSel() {
    var sel = tapSel;
    if (!sel) return;
    tapSel = null;
    if (sel.st) sel.st.last = -1;
    tapInto = sel;
    try { fireOn(sel.st, "onLeave", null); } catch (e) {}
    tapInto = null;
    if (sel.readout && sel.readout.parentNode) sel.readout.parentNode.removeChild(sel.readout);
    if (sel.mark && sel.mark.parentNode) sel.mark.parentNode.removeChild(sel.mark);
    if (sel.box) sel.box.classList.remove("pc-plotbox");
  }
  /* The selected point's PIXELS move on every redraw — a rotation, the overlay
     opening, a new parameter. The INDEX is what the selection means, so it is
     re-looked-up in the (already refreshed) point list and the ring follows it;
     a point that is no longer in the list clears the whole selection rather
     than leaving a ring hanging over nothing. */
  function syncTapSel() {
    var sel = tapSel;
    if (!sel) return;
    if (!sel.canvas.isConnected || !sel.box.isConnected) { clearTapSel(); return; }
    var p = pointOf(sel.st, sel.i);
    if (!p) { clearTapSel(); return; }
    placeMark(sel, p);
  }
  function tapSelect(canvas, st, i, p, evt) {
    var box = plotBoxOf(canvas);
    if (!box) return;
    var changed = !tapSel || tapSel.canvas !== canvas || tapSel.i !== i;
    clearTapSel();                          // one selection on the page at a time
    var sel = { canvas: canvas, st: st, box: box, i: i, readout: null, mark: null };
    tapSel = sel;
    st.last = i;
    tapInto = sel;
    try { fireOn(st, "onHit", i, evt, changed, p); } catch (e) {}
    tapInto = null;
    /* A tap is a hover AND a click. onClick commonly redraws the panel, which
       refreshes st.pts through hover()/update() — so the ring is placed after
       it, from the refreshed list, and again on the next frame once that
       redraw and the strip's own height have settled. */
    if (typeof st.opts.onClick === "function") {
      try { st.opts.onClick(i, evt, p); } catch (e) {}
    }
    if (tapSel !== sel) return;             // the callback moved the selection itself
    syncTapSel();
    raf(function () { syncTapSel(); revealReadout(sel); });
  }

  function hover(canvas, pts, opts) {
    opts = opts || {};
    var st = canvas.__pcHover;
    if (!st) { st = canvas.__pcHover = { last: -1, bound: false }; }
    st.pts = normalizePts(pts);
    st.opts = opts;
    st.radius = Math.max(24, opts.radius || 24);      // ≥24px, never the dot radius
    /* A finger is not a mouse pointer: the tap target is the 32px minimum the
       suite already uses for a control, or the panel's own radius when it asked
       for a bigger one. */
    st.tapRadius = Math.max(32, opts.radius || 0);
    if (tapSel && tapSel.st === st) raf(syncTapSel);   // this panel just redrew

    function allowed(i) {
      var m = st.opts.mask;
      if (!m) return true;
      return typeof m === "function" ? !!m(i) : !!m[i];
    }
    function nearest(evt, radius) {
      var rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      var mx = evt.clientX - rect.left, my = evt.clientY - rect.top;
      var r = radius == null ? st.radius : radius;
      var best = -1, bd = r * r;
      for (var k = 0; k < st.pts.length; k++) {
        var p = st.pts[k];
        if (!allowed(p[2])) continue;
        var dx = p[0] - mx, dy = p[1] - my, d = dx * dx + dy * dy;
        if (d < bd) { bd = d; best = k; }
      }
      return best;
    }
    function call(name) {
      var f = st.opts[name];
      if (typeof f !== "function") return null;
      return f.apply(null, Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments, 1));
    }

    var handle = {
      update: function (next) {
        st.pts = normalizePts(next);
        if (tapSel && tapSel.st === st) syncTapSel();
        return handle;
      },
      setMask: function (m) { st.opts.mask = m; return handle; },
      hit: function () { return st.last; },
      destroy: function () {
        if (tapSel && tapSel.canvas === canvas) clearTapSel();
        canvas.removeEventListener("pointermove", st.move);
        canvas.removeEventListener("pointerleave", st.leave);
        if (st.click) canvas.removeEventListener("click", st.click);
        canvas.__pcHover = null;
      }
    };
    if (st.bound) return handle;
    st.bound = true;
    /* Frozen here, at first bind, and read by the MOUSE branch of st.click
       alone: which canvases answer a mouse click stays exactly what it was
       before the listener became unconditional. */
    st.clickable = typeof opts.onClick === "function";

    st.move = function (evt) {
      /* Touch mode ignores a touch drag outright: that gesture is the page's
         scroll now, and a readout dragged under the finger was the defect. A
         real mouse on the same device still hovers. */
      if (touchMode && evt.pointerType === "touch") return;
      var k = nearest(evt);
      if (k < 0) {
        if (st.last !== -1) { st.last = -1; call("onLeave", evt); }
        return;
      }
      var p = st.pts[k], i = p[2];
      var changed = i !== st.last;
      st.last = i;
      call("onHit", i, evt, changed, p);
    };
    st.leave = function (evt) {
      /* pointerleave fires for a touch pointer at LIFT. Honouring it here is
         precisely what made a phone readout unreadable, so in touch mode the
         selection outlives the finger and only another tap clears it. */
      if (touchMode && evt.pointerType === "touch") return;
      if (st.last !== -1) { st.last = -1; call("onLeave", evt); }
    };
    canvas.addEventListener("pointermove", st.move);
    canvas.addEventListener("pointerleave", st.leave);
    /* NEVER preventDefault, and never on pointerup/touchend: three
       document-level bubble-phase click listeners at the end of this file (the
       tab-scroll policy, the parameter bar's reinstall and the chart overlay's
       reinstall) all depend on the synthetic click still arriving. */
    st.click = function (evt) {
      if (!touchMode) {
        if (!st.clickable) return;                  // the pre-touch-mode contract
        var m = nearest(evt);
        if (m >= 0) call("onClick", st.pts[m][2], evt, st.pts[m]);
        return;
      }
      var k = nearest(evt, st.tapRadius);
      if (k < 0) { clearTapSel(); return; }         // a tap on nothing clears
      tapSelect(canvas, st, st.pts[k][2], st.pts[k], evt);
    };
    canvas.addEventListener("click", st.click);
    return handle;
  }

  /* A tab change swaps the whole panel under the reader, so a strip left over
     from the tab they just left would describe a chart that is no longer on
     screen. Bubble phase, no preventDefault: the tab's own handler and the
     three policies at the end of this file run exactly as before. */
  if (global.document) {
    global.document.addEventListener("click", function (evt) {
      if (!tapSel) return;
      var t = evt.target;
      if (t && t.closest && t.closest('.toptabs')) clearTapSel();
    }, false);
    /* Rotation, the overlay opening, the browser chrome collapsing: all arrive
       as one resize. The ring follows its point through the demo's own redraw
       (immediately for the layout we have, then again once that redraw has
       run). */
    global.addEventListener("resize", function () {
      if (!tapSel) return;
      raf(syncTapSel);
      setTimeout(syncTapSel, 180);
    });
  }

  /* ══ tooltip ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     ── ported: superconductor (showTip/hideTip viewport clamping) + master
     (#tip markup and the opacity convention). Both conventions are driven:
     display for measuring, opacity for the master's .08s fade. The node is
     created only if the page forgot it, and then carries its own minimal
     styles so it is still legible. ───────────────────────────────────────── */
  var tipEl = null;
  function tipNode() {
    if (tipEl && tipEl.isConnected) return tipEl;
    tipEl = document.getElementById("tip");
    if (!tipEl) {
      tipEl = document.createElement("div");
      tipEl.id = "tip";
      tipEl.setAttribute("role", "tooltip");
      tipEl.setAttribute("aria-live", "polite");
      tipEl.style.cssText =
        "position:fixed;pointer-events:none;z-index:1000;max-width:280px;" +
        "padding:9px 12px;border-radius:9px;font-size:12.5px;line-height:1.5;" +
        "background:var(--surface-1);color:var(--text-primary);" +
        "border:1px solid var(--border);box-shadow:0 6px 22px rgba(0,0,0,.16)";
      document.body.appendChild(tipEl);
    }
    return tipEl;
  }
  function tip(html, evt, y) {
    /* THE ONE LINE THAT MOVES THE READOUT ON A PHONE. Every demo's onHit
       already calls PC.tip(html, evt); during a tap that same HTML is docked
       into the plot box's strip instead of being floated under the finger. No
       demo's onHit changes, and #tip is untouched for mouse users. */
    if (tapInto) {
      var docked = readoutFor(tapInto);
      docked.innerHTML = html;
      return docked;
    }
    var el = tipNode();
    el.innerHTML = html;
    el.style.display = "block";
    el.style.opacity = "1";
    var cx = (evt && evt.clientX != null) ? evt.clientX : evt;
    var cy = (evt && evt.clientY != null) ? evt.clientY : y;
    var gap = 14;
    var b = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    el.style.left = Math.max(gap, Math.min(cx + gap, global.innerWidth - b.width - gap)) + "px";
    el.style.top = Math.max(gap, Math.min(cy + gap, global.innerHeight - b.height - gap)) + "px";
    return el;
  }
  function hideTip() {
    /* The mirror of the above: inside a tap, "hide the tooltip" means take the
       docked strip down, which is how a panel's own onLeave clears it. */
    if (tapInto) {
      var docked = tapInto.readout;
      if (docked && docked.parentNode) docked.parentNode.removeChild(docked);
      tapInto.readout = null;
      return;
    }
    var el = tipEl && tipEl.isConnected ? tipEl : document.getElementById("tip");
    if (!el) return;
    el.style.opacity = "0";
    el.style.display = "none";
  }

  /* ── ported: master (the resize `let rt; clearTimeout` idiom), generalised ─ */
  function debounce(fn, ms) {
    var t = null;
    function wrapped() {
      var args = arguments, self = this;
      clearTimeout(t);
      t = setTimeout(function () { t = null; fn.apply(self, args); }, ms == null ? 120 : ms);
    }
    wrapped.cancel = function () { clearTimeout(t); t = null; };
    return wrapped;
  }

  /* ══ linked view state ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
     One state object drives controls, charts, table twins, live readouts and
     conclusions. `params` is an allowlist: only named state fields reach the
     URL, and unknown query parameters (including `theme`) are preserved.

       var view = PC.createViewState({method:"pca", k:6, selected:null}, {
         params: {
           method: {values:["pca","tsne","umap"]},
           k: {type:"integer", min:2, max:40},
           selected: {type:"integer", param:"sample"}
         }
       });
       view.subscribe(function (state) { renderAll(state); }, {immediate:true});
       view.set({k: 8});

     URL values are validated, never silently clamped. Programmatic values are
     normalised to the declared type and rejected when invalid. Defaults are
     removed from the URL so a copied link stays short. ───────────────────── */
  function createViewState(initial, opts) {
    opts = opts || {};
    initial = initial || {};
    var defaults = {};
    Object.keys(initial).forEach(function (k) { defaults[k] = initial[k]; });
    var specs = opts.params || {};
    var listeners = [];

    function own(obj, key) { return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, key); }
    function same(a, b) { return a === b || (a !== a && b !== b); }
    function specFor(key) {
      var s = specs[key];
      if (s === true || s == null) s = {};
      if (typeof s === "string") s = { param: s };
      return s || {};
    }
    function normal(key, value, fallback, fromUrl) {
      var spec = specFor(key), out = value;
      if (value == null && (defaults[key] == null || spec.nullable === true)) {
        return { ok: true, value: null };
      }
      if (typeof spec.parse === "function" && fromUrl) {
        try { out = spec.parse(value, fallback); } catch (e) { return { ok: false, value: fallback }; }
      } else {
        var type = spec.type || (fallback == null ? "string" : typeof fallback);
        if (type === "integer") {
          out = typeof value === "number" ? value : Number(value);
          if (!isFinite(out) || Math.floor(out) !== out) return { ok: false, value: fallback };
        } else if (type === "number") {
          out = typeof value === "number" ? value : Number(value);
          if (!isFinite(out)) return { ok: false, value: fallback };
        } else if (type === "boolean") {
          if (value === true || value === "1" || value === "true" || value === "yes") out = true;
          else if (value === false || value === "0" || value === "false" || value === "no") out = false;
          else return { ok: false, value: fallback };
        } else if (value == null && fallback == null) {
          out = null;
        } else {
          out = String(value);
        }
      }
      if (spec.values && spec.values.indexOf(out) < 0) return { ok: false, value: fallback };
      if (typeof out === "number" && spec.min != null && out < spec.min) return { ok: false, value: fallback };
      if (typeof out === "number" && spec.max != null && out > spec.max) return { ok: false, value: fallback };
      if (typeof spec.validate === "function" && !spec.validate(out)) return { ok: false, value: fallback };
      return { ok: true, value: out };
    }
    function readUrl(base) {
      var next = {};
      Object.keys(base).forEach(function (k) { next[k] = base[k]; });
      if (!global.location || !global.URLSearchParams) return next;
      var query;
      try { query = new URLSearchParams(global.location.search); } catch (e) { return next; }
      Object.keys(specs).forEach(function (key) {
        if (!own(defaults, key)) return;
        var spec = specFor(key), name = spec.param || key;
        if (!query.has(name)) return;
        var parsed = normal(key, query.get(name), defaults[key], true);
        if (parsed.ok) next[key] = parsed.value;
      });
      return next;
    }
    var value = {};
    Object.keys(defaults).forEach(function (k) { value[k] = defaults[k]; });
    if (opts.readUrl !== false) value = readUrl(value);

    function snapshot() {
      var out = {};
      Object.keys(value).forEach(function (k) { out[k] = value[k]; });
      return out;
    }
    function writeUrl() {
      if (opts.writeUrl === false || !global.location || !global.history || !global.URL) return;
      var url;
      try { url = new global.URL(global.location.href); } catch (e) { return; }
      Object.keys(specs).forEach(function (key) {
        if (!own(value, key)) return;
        var spec = specFor(key), name = spec.param || key, current = value[key];
        if (!spec.keepDefault && same(current, defaults[key])) { url.searchParams.delete(name); return; }
        if (current == null || current === "") { url.searchParams.delete(name); return; }
        var encoded;
        try {
          encoded = typeof spec.serialize === "function" ? spec.serialize(current) :
            (typeof current === "boolean" ? (current ? "1" : "0") : String(current));
        } catch (e) { return; }
        if (encoded == null || encoded === "") url.searchParams.delete(name);
        else url.searchParams.set(name, encoded);
      });
      try { global.history.replaceState(global.history.state, "", url.href); } catch (e) { /* file:// may deny history writes */ }
    }
    function emit(changed, meta) {
      var snap = snapshot();
      listeners.slice().forEach(function (fn) { fn(snap, changed.slice(), meta || {}); });
      if (global.CustomEvent && global.dispatchEvent) {
        global.dispatchEvent(new global.CustomEvent("pc:viewstatechange", {
          detail: { state: snap, changed: changed.slice(), source: (meta && meta.source) || "program" }
        }));
      }
    }
    function set(patch, meta) {
      if (typeof patch === "string") {
        var one = {}; one[patch] = arguments[1]; patch = one; meta = arguments[2];
      }
      patch = patch || {};
      var next = snapshot(), changed = [];
      Object.keys(patch).forEach(function (key) {
        if (!own(defaults, key)) return;
        var parsed = normal(key, patch[key], value[key], false);
        if (!parsed.ok || same(parsed.value, value[key])) return;
        next[key] = parsed.value; changed.push(key);
      });
      if (!changed.length) return snapshot();
      value = next;
      if (!meta || meta.url !== false) writeUrl();
      emit(changed, meta);
      return snapshot();
    }
    function subscribe(fn, subOpts) {
      if (typeof fn !== "function") return function () {};
      listeners.push(fn);
      if (subOpts && subOpts.immediate) fn(snapshot(), Object.keys(value), { source: "initial" });
      return function () { var i = listeners.indexOf(fn); if (i >= 0) listeners.splice(i, 1); };
    }
    function reset(keys, meta) {
      var patch = {};
      (keys == null ? Object.keys(defaults) : (Array.isArray(keys) ? keys : [keys]))
        .forEach(function (key) { if (own(defaults, key)) patch[key] = defaults[key]; });
      return set(patch, meta || { source: "reset" });
    }
    return { get: snapshot, set: set, reset: reset, subscribe: subscribe, defaults: function () {
      var out = {}; Object.keys(defaults).forEach(function (k) { out[k] = defaults[k]; }); return out;
    } };
  }

  /* ══ interactive table twins ═════════════════════════════════════════════
     A table remains passive unless a demo opts in. The opted-in table becomes
     a one-column-selection ARIA grid: rows are focusable, arrow/Home/End moves
     focus, Enter/Space selects, click selects, and Escape clears when onClear
     is supplied. Re-rendered tbody content is supported through refresh(). */
  function bindTableRows(table, opts) {
    opts = opts || {};
    if (typeof table === "string") table = document.querySelector(table);
    if (!table) throw new Error("PC.bindTableRows: table not found");
    table.classList.add("interactive-table");
    table.setAttribute("role", "grid");
    var selected = opts.selected;

    function rows() { return Array.prototype.slice.call(table.querySelectorAll("tbody tr")); }
    function keyOf(row, i) {
      return typeof opts.key === "function" ? opts.key(row, i) :
        (row.getAttribute("data-key") != null ? row.getAttribute("data-key") : i);
    }
    function isSelected(key, row, i) {
      if (typeof selected !== "function") return String(key) === String(selected);
      /* A zero-argument function is the documented live value getter used by
         the skeleton (`selected: () => VIEW.get().selected`).  A callback
         declaring arguments is an opt-in row predicate.  Keeping those two
         meanings distinct prevents every row becoming selected when the
         getter returns a truthy sample id. */
      if (selected.length === 0) return String(key) === String(selected());
      return !!selected(key, row, i);
    }
    function refresh(nextSelected) {
      if (arguments.length) selected = nextSelected;
      var list = rows(), focusSet = false;
      list.forEach(function (row, i) {
        var key = keyOf(row, i), on = isSelected(key, row, i);
        row.setAttribute("role", "row");
        row.setAttribute("aria-selected", on ? "true" : "false");
        row.tabIndex = on ? 0 : -1;
        if (on) focusSet = true;
      });
      if (!focusSet && list.length) list[0].tabIndex = 0;
      return api;
    }
    function activate(row, evt) {
      if (!row || row.getAttribute("aria-disabled") === "true") return;
      var list = rows(), i = list.indexOf(row), key = keyOf(row, i);
      if (typeof opts.onSelect === "function") {
        /* Commit the row's ARIA state before the callback. A shared-state
           subscriber may synchronously replace tbody; callers (and assistive
           checks holding the activated node) must still observe that Enter or
           click selected the node they activated. refresh() then reconciles
           the replacement rows with the live selected getter. */
        list.forEach(function (candidate) {
          candidate.setAttribute("aria-selected", candidate === row ? "true" : "false");
          candidate.tabIndex = candidate === row ? 0 : -1;
        });
        opts.onSelect(key, i, row, evt); refresh();
      }
      else { selected = key; refresh(); }
    }
    function click(evt) {
      var row = evt.target.closest ? evt.target.closest("tbody tr") : null;
      if (!row || !table.contains(row)) return;
      activate(row, evt);
    }
    function keydown(evt) {
      var row = evt.target.closest ? evt.target.closest("tbody tr") : null;
      if (!row || !table.contains(row)) return;
      var list = rows(), i = list.indexOf(row), next = i;
      if (evt.key === "ArrowDown") next = Math.min(list.length - 1, i + 1);
      else if (evt.key === "ArrowUp") next = Math.max(0, i - 1);
      else if (evt.key === "Home") next = 0;
      else if (evt.key === "End") next = list.length - 1;
      else if (evt.key === "Enter" || evt.key === " ") { evt.preventDefault(); activate(row, evt); return; }
      else if (evt.key === "Escape" && typeof opts.onClear === "function") {
        evt.preventDefault();
        /* onClear may synchronously replace tbody (linked plots commonly
           redraw their table twins).  Preserve the user's logical row as the
           sole roving tab stop after that redraw instead of leaving focus on
           a tabindex=-1 row while a different selected row owns tabindex=0. */
        var keepKey = keyOf(row, i);
        opts.onClear(evt);
        refresh();
        var current = rows(), keep = null;
        current.forEach(function (candidate, at) {
          if (String(keyOf(candidate, at)) === String(keepKey)) keep = candidate;
          candidate.tabIndex = -1;
        });
        if (keep) { keep.tabIndex = 0; keep.focus(); }
        else if (current.length) { current[0].tabIndex = 0; current[0].focus(); }
        return;
      } else return;
      evt.preventDefault();
      list.forEach(function (r) { r.tabIndex = -1; });
      if (list[next]) { list[next].tabIndex = 0; list[next].focus(); }
    }
    table.addEventListener("click", click);
    table.addEventListener("keydown", keydown);
    var api = {
      refresh: refresh,
      select: function (value) { selected = value; return refresh(); },
      destroy: function () { table.removeEventListener("click", click); table.removeEventListener("keydown", keydown); }
    };
    return refresh();
  }

  /* ══ public drawing API ════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
  var PC = {
    version: "1.3.0",
    css: css,
    alias: ALIAS,
    isDark: isDark,
    setTheme: setTheme,
    registerThemePainter: registerThemePainter,
    repaintThemePainters: repaintThemePainters,
    font: { sizes: FONT_SIZE, family: fontFamily, tick: tickFont, emph: emphFont },
    rampColor: rampColor,
    rampScale: rampScale,
    heatColor: heatColor,
    heatScale: heatScale,
    divColor: divColor,
    divScale: divScale,
    inkOn: inkOn,
    hex2rgb: hex2rgb,
    toOklab: toOklab,
    fromOklab: fromOklab,
    fit: fit,
    PAD: PAD,
    scales: scales,
    boxOf: boxOf,
    frame: frame,
    tickText: tickText,
    drawAxes: drawAxes,
    fmt: fmt,
    extent: extent,
    pad10: pad10,
    quantile: quantile,
    hover: hover,
    tip: tip,
    hideTip: hideTip,
    touchMode: function () { return touchMode; },
    plotBoxOf: plotBoxOf,
    PLOT_BOXES: PLOT_BOXES,
    clearSelection: clearTapSel,
    selection: function () {
      return tapSel ? { canvas: tapSel.canvas, index: tapSel.i } : null;
    },
    debounce: debounce,
    createViewState: createViewState,
    bindTableRows: bindTableRows
  };

  global.PC = PC;
  if (typeof module === "object" && module.exports) module.exports = PC;
})(typeof globalThis !== "undefined" ? globalThis : this);
